children: Gold declines in early Asian trade. The precious metal is likely to remain weighed down by higher crude oil prices keeping inflationary pressures in place and reinforcing hawkish monetary-policy expectations, says Bas Kooijman of DHF Capital S.A. in a note. Investors are likely to watch October's Federal Reserve meeting for hints on the U.S. interest rate outlook, he says. "Although the Fed is widely expected to leave rates steady, attention will likely remain on clues regarding another possible increase in December," he adds. A higher interest-rate environment typically drags down the non-interest-yielding yellow metal. Spot gold is down 0.2% at $4,117.90 an ounce.(megan.cheah@wsj.com)
